dimensions.label: Motion adherence
evidence: how many caregivers do you have active right now, and roughly how many of your clients are private pay versus on some kind of managed care contract?
dimensions.tip: Continue leading every demo with a quick discovery check-in before pitching, but tighten the transition into value tied specifically to what was just learned.

dimensions.label: Discovery quality
evidence: We're at about 60 caregivers, maybe 140 clients. Split's roughly 70% private pay, 30% through a couple of MCO contracts.
dimensions.tip: Dig deeper into timeline, budget authority, and decision process (e.g., what does the partner need to approve, when do they want to go live) rather than just caseload mix.

dimensions.label: Talk / listen balance
dimensions.tip: Aim for more listening — open with questions and let the buyer talk.

dimensions.label: Buying-signal detection & handling
evidence: I do need something concrete before I bring this to my partner. She's going to ask 'what's the ROI' in the first thirty seconds.
dimensions.tip: Explicitly ask what budget range or timeline the partner has in mind so the proposal can be scoped to close, not just informative.

dimensions.label: Objection handling
evidence: My worry is my caregivers, honestly — some of them are older, less tech-savvy, and I can already hear them saying 'is this replacing me'
dimensions.tip: Keep pairing objection responses with a customer proof point (e.g., Diana story) to make the resolution concrete rather than anecdotal.

dimensions.label: Proof-point fidelity
evidence: that's a stat from Sensi's customer base broadly, not something I'm promising you specifically will hit
dimensions.tip: When citing the 35% stat, proactively offer the source/context up front rather than waiting for the prospect to push back.

dimensions.label: Next-step specificity
evidence: I'll put it together and follow up next week
dimensions.tip: Lock a specific date/time for the follow-up call and proposal delivery instead of a vague 'next week.'

flags.evidence: We've seen agencies using this pick up 35% more billable hours just from documentation that actually reflects the care being delivered

recommendations.title: 35% Billable Hours Methodology One-Pager
recommendations.why: Prospect explicitly asked for the source behind the 35% stat before bringing it to her partner; a sourced breakdown would speed trust and proposal credibility.

recommendations.title: Caregiver Adoption / Non-Monitoring Talk Track
recommendations.why: Denise raised the caregiver 'is this spying on me' objection which was handled well verbally but a written positioning guide would help her sell it internally.

recommendations.title: ROI Calculator Tied to Caseload Mix
recommendations.why: Buyer needs a concrete, agency-specific ROI figure for her partner meeting rather than the general case-study stat.

summary: Solid discovery-first demo with strong, honest objection handling (caregiver adoption, dementia clients) and appropriate caveats on the 35% stat. However, next steps remain vague ('next week') without a firm date, and discovery stopped short of budget/timeline/decision process needed to qualify this as a real opportunity.
